localHost.hostName: Add here the Hostname of the local device
localHost.userHome: Add here the working directory of the local device. Backups land in <userHome>/backup
localHost.userName: Add here the Username of the local device

knownHosts: Add here the path to your knownHosts file. cattleServer maintains it: see hostKeyPolicy
logDir: Optional. Where the service log and the per-application logs go. Defaults to <localHost.userHome>/cattleServer-Logs. The service log is also how the scheduler remembers the last backup, so moving it makes cattleServer take one immediately
hostKeyPolicy: Optional, one of 'accept-new' (default) or 'strict'. accept-new runs ssh-keyscan on a host that is not in knownHosts yet and adds what it answers; strict never writes to the file. Neither ever replaces an entry that is already there, so a host whose key changed always fails
checkEvery: Optional, minutes between two passes over the apps (default 30). This bounds how late a backup can be, not how often one happens: each app has its own backupFrequency, and a pass only acts on the ones that are due. A pass that finds nothing due costs one log file read
startupDelay: Optional, minutes to wait before the first pass (default 30). Zero makes the first pass happen at startup, which on a machine with no log yet means backing up immediately, because nothing records a previous backup
progressEvery: Optional, seconds between two progress lines while a transfer is running (default 30). rsync reports several times a second, so this keeps a large transfer to a handful of lines. The line saying the transfer finished is always reported
verifyEvery: Optional, hours between re-reading one backup and checking it against the manifest written when it was made. Absent never does. This is what turns 'it was written correctly' into 'it is still correct'; it costs reading a whole backup, so it is off unless asked for
alertCommand: Optional, shell command run when an application passes its alertAfter, with the detail on standard input. Logging is not warning: a service failing for a month has been saying so in a file nobody reads. One command per window, not per pass, and a successful backup resets it

appConfig.name: Add here the name of your application, this will be used to create the logfile, sqlfile and backup directory. Renaming it makes cattleServer lose track of the last backup and take one immediately
appConfig.structure: Add here the uploads directory of your application in the remote host. It arrives in the backup under its own basename, so /loads lands as loads

databaseConfig.name: Add here the username to use in postgresql
databaseConfig.structure: Add here the name of the database structure

backupFrequency.unit: Add here the time unit of the recursive backup, (default = Hours). Means 8 Hours

deleteFrequency.unit: Add here the time unit for how long a backup is kept, (default = Days). Means 10 Days. Every backup older than this is removed, oldest first, subject to keepAtLeast

keyDirectory.name: Add here the name of your SSH key, without the extension. The .pub is read from the same directory
keyDirectory.structure: Add here the path of your SSH key, without the filename

remoteHost.hostName: Add here the Hostname of the remote device
remoteHost.userHome: Add here the working directory of the remote device
remoteHost.userName: Add here the Username of the remote device

serviceConfig.portNumber: Add here the port will be used to connect to the remote host (def 22)
serviceConfig.keepAtLeast: Optional, how many backups must survive whatever deleteFrequency would remove (default 2). Deletion goes by date and runs whether or not the backup before it succeeded, so on its own it empties the directory after a week of failing backups. Two means a corrupt newest backup still leaves one behind it. Zero restores deletion that only looks at the calendar
serviceConfig.remoteRsyncPath: Optional, where rsync lives on the remote host. Only needed when it is not on the PATH a non-interactive 'ssh host command' gets, which on NixOS is a short one
serviceConfig.alertAfter: Optional, hours without a successful backup before alertCommand is run. Absent never alerts. Set it comfortably above backupFrequency so an ordinary late run does not raise one
serviceConfig.hostKeys: Optional. The remote host's public keys, as knownHosts lines or bare '<type> <base64>' pairs. Declared keys are installed as they are, without asking the network, which is what makes hostKeyPolicy 'strict' usable
serviceConfig.hostKeyFingerprint: Optional, 'SHA256:...'. A scanned key has to match it to be trusted. Only consulted when the host is scanned, not when hostKeys are declared

databaseConfig.structure: to configure other times backup, too.
